test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 25 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
**Consider the following statements regarding recent India-Maldives bilateral developments:****1. India announced a financial assistance package of USD 1.4 billion to Maldives during President Solih's 2018 visit.
2. The 6th Joint Commission Meeting (JCM) in 2019 included signing MoUs between the Financial Intelligence Units (FIUs) of both countries.
3. In 2020, India and Maldives signed an agreement for mutual support in climate risk insurance for island territories.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?**
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **December 2018**, during the state visit of Maldives President **Ibrahim Mohamed Solih** to **India**, the Indian government announced a comprehensive financial assistance package of **USD 1.4 billion**. This package was designed to assist the **Maldives** in its socio-economic development and included **budgetary support**, **currency swap agreements**, and **concessional lines of credit**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **6th Joint Commission Meeting (JCM)** between **India** and the **Maldives** was held in **New Delhi** on **13 December 2019**. It was co-chaired by India's External Affairs Minister and the Maldivian Foreign Minister. During this meeting, multiple **Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs)** were signed, including one specifically for cooperation between the **Financial Intelligence Units (FIUs)** of the two countries to strengthen the framework against **money laundering** and **terrorism financing**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• In **2020**, the bilateral relationship was characterized by the **USD 500 million** assistance for the **Greater Male Connectivity Project (GMCP)** and a **USD 250 million** budgetary support to mitigate the impact of **COVID-19**. There is no historical record of a specific agreement signed in **2020** regarding "mutual support in climate risk insurance for island territories" as a primary bilateral development between these two nations. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The diplomatic relationship between the two nations follows the **"India First"** policy of **Maldives** and the **"Neighborhood First"** policy of **India**, aiming for **security and growth for all in the region (SAGAR)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geopolitical Significance:** The **Maldives** is strategically located in the **Indian Ocean**, sitting astride vital **Sea Lines of Communication (SLOCs)** through which a significant portion of world trade and energy supplies pass. It is separated from India's **Minicoy Island** by the **Eight Degree Channel**.
 
• **Operation Cactus (1988):** This was a landmark military intervention where **Indian Armed Forces** assisted the **Maldivian government** in neutralizing a **coup attempt** by mercenaries. This established **India** as a reliable security partner in the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**.
 
• **Operation Neer (2014):** Under this operation, **India** dispatched heavy-lift aircraft and naval ships carrying **bottled water** to **Male** after the city's only **desalination plant** caught fire, demonstrating India's role as a **first responder**.
 
• **Greater Male Connectivity Project (GMCP):** Launched with Indian support, it is the **largest infrastructure project** in the **Maldives**, consisting of a **6.74 km bridge and causeway link** connecting the capital **Male** with the neighboring islands of **Villingili**, **Gulhifalhu**, and **Thilafushi**.
 
• **Economic Cooperation:** **India** is one of the largest **trading partners** of the **Maldives**. In **2021**, India emerged as the **3rd largest** trade partner. The bilateral trade includes exports of **rice**, **spices**, **fruits**, **vegetables**, and **poultry products** from India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Defence Ties:** **India** provides the largest number of **training opportunities** for the **Maldivian National Defence Force (MNDF)**, meeting around **70%** of their total training requirements. Joint exercises like **"Ekuverin"** and **"Dosti"** are held regularly.
 
• **Health Cooperation:** During the **COVID-19 pandemic**, the **Maldives** was the first country to receive **Made-in-India vaccines** (Covishield) in **January 2021** under the **Vaccine Maitri** initiative.
 
• **International Forums:** Both countries are members of the **South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)**, the **Commonwealth**, and the **Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA)**. India supported the **Maldives'** bid for the **Presidency** of the **76th session** of the **United Nations General Assembly** in **2021**.
